newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS - up slightly, Colo. deal reprices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS - up slightly, Colo. deal reprices.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were slightly higher in quiet action, as the new issue market focused on midday repricings in the negotiated sector.

Lehman Brothers said it repriced Thursday's largest new deal, an $811 million bond issue from Arapahoe County, Colo.'s E-470 Public Highway Authority. Lehman said it lowered yields in several maturities.
PaineWebber Inc won the largest competitive offering, a $101 million Wisconsin general obligation issue which the firm reoffered at 5.15 percent in 2018.
Muni secondary traders said price increases were as high as 1/4 point in spots, but gains are hard to come by given lots of new supply and waning demand at the new yield levels.

U.S. Treasury prices see-sawed in early action, as some analysts said fears of a strong July jobs report Friday were adding volatility to the market. The government long bond rose 2/32 to 104 at midday, to yield 6.32 percent.
Analysts said they expected the jobs report to show a 193,000 increase in non-farm payrolls and a 4.9 percent unemployment rate.

In economic data released Thursday, first-time jobless claims for the latest week fell to the lowest level in more than 23 years. The data showed claims slipping to 277,000 in the week ended July 26 from 299,000 in the previous week. That undershot Wall Street economists' consensus forecast for 306,000 of claims.

The Commerce Department said the second quarter Gross Domestic Product rose 2.2 percent compared to a revised 4.9 percent in the first quarter. Economists surveyed by Reuters had expected a 1.9 percent gain.
In the muni secondary market, bids on Fairfax County Water Authority, Va., 5.0s of 2029 were up one basis point from Wednesday, to 5.29 percent.
Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC 5-3/4s of 2027 were also one basis point higher, at 5.27 percent.
September municipal bond contracts climbed 3/32 to 122-5/32, while September Treasury bond futures gained 2/32 to 116-14/32. The MOB spread widened to 183 ticks from 182 at the close on Wednesday.
